executive_summary: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5695, 35 pips (0.61%) below the 52-week high of 0.57299 printed on 28 July 2026 and at the 95th percentile of its 52-week range of 0.50741–0.57299. The pair has risen 0.90% over one month, 1.54% over three months, 4.07% over six months and 8.26% over twelve, and is 12.2% above the October 2025 low — a persistent, low-volatility grind higher rather than a spike. The dominant bilateral fact is the widest policy differential available anywhere in the G10+SGD complex: the RBA at 4.35% against an SNB at 0.00% delivers +435bp of annualised carry against a cross realising roughly 5.6% volatility, a carry-to-vol ratio near 0.78 that is eight times what AUD/USD offers. Critically, this differential is structurally protected on the quote side in a way no other AUD cross enjoys: the SNB's own June conditional inflation forecast of 0.6%/0.6%/0.7% is explicitly built on a 0.00% policy rate through 2028, so where the AUD dossier's strategic worry is peer central banks converging upward on the RBA, the Swiss leg simply cannot converge. That is the single most important divergence from the standalone views — the AUD dossier is strategically Neutral because Norges Bank, the Fed and the RBNZ are catching up, and none of those currencies is the quote leg here. Against that, this is the purest risk-proxy pair in the G10 — the highest-beta currency long against the ultimate haven — and it is expensive: PPP-style estimates from both dossiers put fair value between 0.5061 and 0.5336, making spot 6.7% to 12.5% rich, with Australia's real effective exchange rate at the 97th percentile against a Swiss REER at the 40th. We are tactically Bullish at conviction 4 (weighted score +0.545) and strategically Bullish at conviction 3 (weighted score +0.260), with the explicit caveat that the entire return is carry harvest plus a bounded spot drift, sitting on top of a fat left tail that opens the moment realised volatility breaks the carry regime.

market_context.valuation_assessment: The pair is expensive on every long-run measure available, and the two dossiers disagree only on the magnitude. The AUD dossier's REER-differential method puts AUD/CHF fair value at 0.5336, implying spot is 6.7% rich; the CHF dossier's mirror calculation puts fair value at 0.5061, implying spot is 12.5% rich. The underlying driver is a 57-percentile gap in real effective exchange rates: Australia's BIS real broad REER printed 115.92 in June 2026, +9.8% year-on-year and at the 97th percentile of the available window, while Switzerland's printed 101.69 at only the 40th percentile and 0.1% below its own window mean. In plain terms, the base currency of this pair is the most expensive currency in the bloc in real terms and the quote currency is the cheapest-relative-to-its-own-history among the majors — a structural argument for the pair to fall, not rise. What is priced at 0.5695 is a permanent 435bp differential, a permanent Swiss zero-rate commitment, and a risk regime that never breaks. Valuation is not actionable inside four weeks but is the single reason strategic conviction is capped at 3 and the reason the strategic target does not extend beyond 0.5800.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime since December 2025 has been a textbook carry-on, haven-off grind in which the pair's two legs have been driven by entirely separate engines that happen to point the same way. On the AUD side, an energy-led terms-of-trade windfall (JKM LNG at US$21.43/mmBtu, +78% year-on-year; Newcastle coal at US$134/t; copper up 46%) has supported the highest policy rate in the bloc. On the CHF side, the market has re-designated the franc from a haven into the world's cheapest funding currency after the SNB published a three-year forecast conditioned on a 0.00% rate, with gold down 17.9% over six months confirming the whole haven complex is in drawdown. The last twenty sessions specifically: a steady advance from 0.5554 on 2 July through a decisive break above 0.5670 on 20 July, acceleration to the 0.57299 high on 28 July, a 0.98% single-day reversal on 29 July, four sessions of tight consolidation between 0.56462 and 0.56972, and a recovery to 0.57042 on 4 August — a pullback-and-retest, not a top.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The policy differential is +435bp (RBA 4.35% minus SNB 0.00%), the widest bilateral gap in the entire G10+SGD matrix and the widest of any AUD cross or any CHF cross. The term structure is wider still — Australian 2Y at 4.57% against Swiss 2Y at 0.14% is +443bp, and ACGB 10Y at 4.93% against Swiss 10Y at 0.475% is +445.5bp — telling you the market prices further divergence, not convergence. SARON fixed at -0.04% means Swiss overnight money is negative in practice, and the SNB's threshold-factor cut from 15 to 13.5 effective 1 August 2026 mechanically expands remunerated reserves at policy minus 25bp. The carry-to-vol ratio of 0.79 against 60-day realised volatility (0.69 against estimated 3M implied) makes AUD/CHF the highest risk-adjusted carry cross available in the developed-market complex, exceeding AUD/USD (0.10), AUD/NZD (0.33), AUD/JPY (0.46) and AUD/SGD (0.65) — and that arithmetic, not any independent view on Australia or Switzerland, is what has driven the pair 12.2% higher since October. Carry is working on all four classic markers (VIX 17.09, US HY OAS 281-284bp, S&P near highs, cross realised vol 5.5%), but the regime's persistence is the entire trade, since a VIX above 18 historically unwinds carry trades and drives JPY and CHF higher, and VIX at 17.09 is one print away from that threshold. The forward curve embeds 4.54-4.60% annualised depreciation, exceeding the 435bp policy gap by 20-25bp because the money-market differential is wider than the policy differential and because of the unobservable cross-currency basis, meaning a long AUD/CHF forward buys the pair at a discount and earns the full 129.8 pips over six months if spot is unchanged — a carry harvest first, directional view second.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The differential is +435bp and there is no scheduled mechanism inside the tactical window by which it can narrow, because the only central bank meeting in the window belongs to the base currency. The RBA decides on 11 August with a full Statement on Monetary Policy, and market pricing is roughly a coin flip on a 25bp hike after the 29 July CPI undershoot at 3.8% headline with the trimmed mean flat at 3.6% — meaning the distribution of outcomes for the differential runs from unchanged at +435bp to +460bp, with zero probability of compression. The SNB does not meet until 24 September, well outside the window, and its June conditional inflation forecast of 0.6%/0.6%/0.7% is constructed on an explicit assumption of a 0.00% policy rate throughout, so the quote leg is pinned by publication. That is the transmission mechanism and it is unusually clean: the pair's carry is a one-sided option on the base currency, and the option premium is the 22-24bp of hiking already priced into the Australian 52-week note at 4.59%. Pricing is broadly consistent with the differential — the 6M forward discount of 4.56% annualised is what a 435bp gap plus a 20bp money-market wedge should produce — so the mispricing here is not in the level but in the persistence, where forwards implicitly assume the gap holds and we think there is a modest upward skew to it. The residual 12-25bp of hawkish premium sitting in the CHF front end on stale OIS pricing is a second source of tactical upside for the pair as it decays toward the SNB's own zero assumption.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: This is where the bilateral lens produces a conclusion neither dossier reaches on its own. The AUD dossier is strategically Neutral on rates because every peer is converging upward — the Fed drifting toward 4.00%, Norges Bank's own path just above 4.5% at end-2026, the RBNZ heading to 3.00-3.25%, the ECB roughly 70% priced for September. Not one of those currencies is the quote leg of this pair. The SNB is the single central bank in the benchmark set that is structurally excluded from the convergence trade, because its own published conditional forecast assumes 0.00% through 2028 and sits comfortably inside the 0-2% price-stability band at every horizon point, giving it no internally consistent reason to move. Even in the AUD dossier's own bear case, where Australia loses its rate crown to Norway and the AU-US gap compresses to +35bp, the AU-CH gap compresses by exactly zero. The realistic strategic range for the differential is +410bp (if the RBA delivers CBA's two 2027 cuts early, which is outside the window) to +460bp (one further hike), against a central case of unchanged at +435bp. Transmission over six months is through the forward curve and through real-money allocation: a 4.56% annualised forward discount means any strategic short of this pair must beat a 4.56% hurdle, and the flow evidence is that global carry books are lengthening rather than reducing franc-funded exposure. The counterweight is that a differential this wide has historically not prevented the pair from falling when volatility breaks, which is why confidence is 68 rather than 75.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential is extraordinary: Australian headline CPI at 3.8% against Swiss headline at 0.5% is a 330bp gap, and core is identical at 3.6% trimmed mean against 0.3% SFSO core inflation 1. Growth diverges the same way — 2.5% year-on-year in Australia against 0.59% in Switzerland on the OECD-harmonised basis. Nominally that combination sustains the rate differential, and the real-rate comparison sharpens it: Australia's real policy rate is +0.55% (4.35% less 3.8%) while Switzerland's is -0.50% (0.00% less 0.5%), so Australia offers a 105bp real premium as well as a 435bp nominal one, which is the more durable driver. Asymmetric data sensitivity is the tactical point and it is severe: because the SNB is pinned to zero regardless of what Swiss CPI does within a 0.3-0.9% corridor, Swiss data has almost no transmission to this pair, while Australian data transmits fully through the RBA reaction function. The August window contains the Swiss July CPI in the first week and the Australian July Labour Force on 20 August, and only the second can move the differential. The tactical skew is bullish for the pair because the Swiss print faces an unfavourable energy base effect as the March-April Brent spike drops out of the annual comparison, and a sub-0.4% Swiss headline would revive negative-rate speculation that the market has stopped pricing — a franc negative with no offsetting Australian mechanism.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the inflation differential flips from a support to a drag, and this is the cleanest analytical reversal in the report. A 330bp inflation gap compounding means the pair must fall roughly 3.3% a year in nominal terms to hold its real exchange rate constant — which is exactly why AUD/CHF sits 6.7% to 12.5% above PPP-style fair value and why every long-horizon model forecast in the market points down: one deep-learning model puts AUD/CHF at 0.5242 after a year, a 0.76% decline, and longer-run statistical projections put the average near 0.4685 by end-2030. That is not a forecast we accept for the six-month window, but it is the arithmetic of persistent inflation differentials, and it operates against us. On growth, the picture genuinely offsets: Australia faces 75bp of 2026 tightening still transmitting into a bottom-decile consumer-sentiment reading of 83.9, while Switzerland faces a dated, quantified tariff shock — Section 232 pharmaceutical duties at a capped 15% rate that took effect on 31 July for Annex III companies and extend to all importers on 29 September — with EY putting Swiss 2026 growth at 0.6% against the SNB's 'around 1%'. Two decelerating economies with a 330bp inflation gap and a 191bp growth gap that is narrowing produces no directional signal. Neutral is honest.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This pair is the market's most direct expression of global risk appetite in the developed-market complex, more so than AUD/JPY now that the BoJ is at 1.00% and the SNB is at zero. AUD/CHF is conventionally used as a carry trade and often used as a measuring stick for global economic performance, and the AUD leg is heavily influenced by commodity prices while the CHF leg is a safe haven that rises in times of uncertainty, sending AUD/CHF down. Every observable risk metric is currently supportive: VIX at 17.09, US investment-grade OAS near 80bp, high-yield OAS at 281-284bp, the S&P 500 around 7,467-7,490 with the Dow posting a fourth consecutive winning month, and copper at approximately US$14,195/t up 46% year-on-year near a 2026 record. The single most informative bilateral cross-asset signal is gold: at US$4,054/oz it is down 12.14% over three months and 17.94% over six from the February peak of US$5,277.88, and because CHF and gold share a debasement-and-uncertainty demand function rather than a trade link, that drawdown is direct evidence the haven complex is being liquidated. The correlation structure is intact rather than broken — the franc is still behaving as a haven; there is simply no risk-off to trade. Transmission is immediate and two-legged: risk-on lifts AUD through the commodity and equity channels while simultaneously depressing CHF through the funding channel, so the pair captures both sides of the same impulse rather than one.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: The strategic assessment requires resolving an apparent contradiction: the AUD dossier is strategically Bearish on risk for AUD, and the CHF dossier is strategically Bearish on risk for CHF. Those cannot both be true for the pair, and the resolution is that they describe different scenarios rather than the same one. In the modal 50% path the carry regime persists, the franc continues to be sold as funding and the pair grinds higher — the CHF dossier's case. In the 25% left tail a volatility shock breaks the regime, and then the two legs compound rather than offset: AUD falls as the highest-beta G10 currency while CHF rallies as the funding leg being repaid, so AUD/CHF is the single most negatively convex pair in the developed complex. A quick rally in the funding currency can wipe out gains and cause rapid unwinds, and high volatility or a drop in the higher-yielding currency has the same effect, and the franc jumped as much as 3.5% over two days when stock markets tumbled in the August 2024 analogue. The SNB's removal of its euro peg in 2015 triggered a flash rally in the franc that wiped out years of carry trade gains. The expected value across the distribution is mildly positive, but the skew is decisively negative, and forcing a directional stance on a 0.08-weighted factor whose distribution is this asymmetric would misrepresent the analysis. Neutral with documented negative convexity is the correct score.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Netting the two legs produces a genuinely neutral read rather than a default one. Leveraged funds are long +24,788 AUD contracts and short -8,897 CHF contracts — aligned, and therefore amplifying for a long AUD/CHF position, with an implied overlap of roughly US$1.4bn. Asset managers are short -35,144 AUD and short -37,558 CHF — almost perfectly offsetting, and therefore muting. Percentiles say neither leg is stretched: AUD net specs at roughly the 50th percentile of the trailing year against reversal thresholds near ±80,000 contracts, and the CHF blend at the 52nd percentile with asset managers close to their least-short reading of the cached window. The combined pair position is therefore mid-range, and the transmission is that there is neither a squeeze to fuel a further leg higher nor a crowded long to flush. The behavioural evidence is more informative than the levels and it points the same way on both legs: AUD leveraged longs were cut 36.6% over five weeks while AUD rose 1.34%, and CHF leveraged shorts were covered from -9,500 to -8,897 while the franc fell 0.90% against the euro. Both legs saw speculative positioning move against the direction of spot, which means the pair's advance is being driven by real-money and structural funding flow that CME data cannot see.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Strategically the visible data remains a non-signal but the invisible flow is the whole story, and it runs in the pair's favour with a dangerous shape. The structural development of this cycle is the franc's reassignment from haven to preferred global funding currency, explicitly because franc funding is cheaper than yen funding and avoids Bank of Japan intervention risk. 'The Swiss franc is back as a funding currency,' in the words of one overlay manager, and carry-vol ratios have made borrowing in Swiss francs the more attractive funding choice since January 2024, even against pairs with wider raw differentials. That flow does not appear in CME futures; it appears in cross-border bank lending and the FX swap market, and it means the true short-franc position in crosses like AUD/CHF is materially larger than the US$1.38bn visible, held by participants with longer holding periods and less weekly volatility sensitivity. The bilateral consequence is a sticky position that is slow to unwind but that exits through a very narrow door if it does. On the base leg, the pro-cyclical Australian superannuation hedging channel (roughly A$4.3 trillion of assets) is currently AUD-supportive with global equities near highs and reverses in precisely the same scenario. Two structural flow channels supporting the pair, both pro-cyclical, both reversing on the same trigger — that correlation is the strategic fragility and it is invisible in the positioning data.

Commodity prices bullish, external stocks bearish, both large: Neutral.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The guidance divergence here is the widest in the G10 and it runs one way. The RBA has delivered 75bp of tightening across three 2026 meetings, retained the explicit clause 'including increasing the cash rate target further if required' in a unanimous June hold, and had Governor Bullock repeat on 28 July that the Board is prepared to act including by increasing the cash rate further if needed. The SNB, in the same window, published a three-year conditional inflation forecast constructed on an explicit 0.00% policy-rate assumption and stated an 'increased willingness to intervene in the foreign exchange market' to counter rapid and excessive franc appreciation — guidance that is one-directional against its own currency. 'The Swiss National Bank wants a weaker Swiss franc' is now a consensus reading of that language, and SNB credibility and its readiness to intervene influence the franc more than the policy rate, and that same intervention stance caps how far the franc is allowed to appreciate. For the pair the transmission is direct and asymmetric: one central bank has pre-committed to defend against strength in its currency while the other has pre-committed to the option of raising the yield on its currency. Sequencing favours the pair inside the window — the RBA meets on 11 August with a full SoMP and press conference, the SNB not until 24 September — so the only guidance event in the tactical window belongs to the leg that can only surprise hawkishly. Credibility is high on both sides, which matters: markets believe the SNB will hold at zero (28 of 29 forecasters) and believe the RBA follows through on stated reaction functions, so the guidance gap is priced but the conditionality of the RBA's clause is only about half priced.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.12 strategic weight this becomes the second-largest positive contributor, and the reason is that guidance is the mechanism by which the franc's structural role was reassigned. A central bank that pre-commits to inaction for three years removes its currency's optionality entirely, and a currency without policy optionality that also has the lowest yield in its peer group is definitionally a funding currency — which is exactly what late-July reporting that SNB insiders see zero until end-2027 accomplished. The rate difference makes the franc the perfect funding currency for carry trades as volatility falls, a classic setup reminiscent of the pre-2008 era when the yen played a similar role. On the base side the RBA offers the clearest and most credible policy signal in the bloc at the highest policy rate in the bloc, with the strongest 2026 follow-through record and no leadership transition. Over six months the pair therefore benefits from a credibility differential in both directions: the RBA is believed when it says it might hike, and the SNB is believed when it says it will not — and both beliefs widen or preserve the differential. The strategic risk is specific: the RBA's May baseline assumed the conflict would be resolved and fuel prices would fall, and serial forecast revisions across the August and November SoMPs would erode the market's willingness to extrapolate RBA guidance. The mirror risk is that a Swiss CPI print above 1.0% with core above 0.6% would force the SNB to revise its 2027 path, which is the one event that restores franc optionality and flips this factor.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The dominant event affecting both legs is the same one — the Strait of Hormuz disruption, now in its sixth month after the 17 June memorandum of understanding collapsed on 8 July and the naval blockade was reimposed around 13-14 July — and its bilateral effect is genuinely two-sided, which is the point. Escalation raises LNG, coal and crude prices, which is a direct terms-of-trade positive for the third-largest LNG exporter and a direct terms-of-trade negative for a pure energy importer, so the price channel is unambiguously bullish for the pair. But escalation past a threshold flips the risk channel, and the risk channel moves this pair harder than the price channel because it moves both legs at once. The bilateral threshold we identify is Brent sustaining above roughly US$115: below it the market treats energy as an inflation variable and the pair rises; above it the market reclassifies it as a risk event and the franc catches a haven bid that overwhelms Australia's export gain. That inversion is specific to this pair — it does not exist for AUD/CAD or AUD/NOK, where both legs are energy exporters — and it is the most useful single insight in this factor. On the quote side, the dated event has just landed: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs at a capped 15% Swiss rate took effect on 31 July for Annex III companies, with commentary already attributing short-term franc pressure to the combination of new US tariffs and weak Swiss exports. Netting a dated, capped, franc-negative trade shock against an undated, uncapped, franc-positive geopolitical tail gives no directional edge over four weeks.

That concavity caps rather than reverses the tactical stance.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over six months the event distribution for this pair is unusually poorly shaped, and it is worth stating the two branches precisely. If Hormuz escalates further, energy prices rise and Australia's terms of trade improve, but the accompanying growth shock, equity drawdown and credit widening hit the pair through the channel to which it has the highest combined beta in the G10 — the RBA's own adverse scenario has an LNG price of US$30/mmBtu lifting Australia's trade-weighted index while leaving GDP 0.5% lower by mid-2028, and the franc would be the primary beneficiary. If Hormuz resolves, energy prices fall back, Australia loses the terms-of-trade support that has underwritten the pair's advance, and the risk-on relief accrues disproportionately to energy importers — which is exactly what Switzerland is. The pair therefore loses relative ground in the good scenario and absolute ground in the bad one, which is a concave payoff. Layered beneath it is the China channel, where Q2 GDP at 4.3% was the weakest since Q4 2022, the July NBS manufacturing PMI fell back into contraction at 49.2, and the PBoC has not cut the LPR, the reverse repo or the RRR at any point in 2026 — a one-sided negative for the base leg with no offsetting Swiss exposure. The 10 November US-China tariff truce expiry falls inside the window and is a further one-sided risk. Against all of that sits the quote leg's own dated negative: the 29 September full extension of pharma tariffs and the phased USD 200bn Swiss investment outflow into the United States. Balanced, at low weight.

Australia's position is strong but not scarce in the same way — the AAA is intact and the commodity revenue overshoot is real, but state government borrowing has risen materially (particularly Victoria) and structural Commonwealth spending pressures from the NDIS, aged care, health and defence are the identified medium-term rating risks. It is a genuine directional lean, not a tradeable view.

risk_reward.asymmetry_assessment: Including carry the distribution is favourably skewed at roughly 2:1, but that ratio is manufactured almost entirely by the 4.56% annualised forward discount rather than by any expected spot move — on spot alone the trade is unfavourable at 0.43:1. The strategic long AUD/CHF is a carry harvest with a bounded expected spot gain and an unbounded tail loss; fiscal quality on the Swiss side and the 13.45pp current-account differential bound the upside at roughly 0.5950, but nothing bounds the downside except the SNB's stated willingness to sell francs, and the January 2015 precedent establishes that SNB behaviour is not a reliable stop.

consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast: Model-based forecasters cluster near 0.5710-0.5800 by end-2026 (one puts AUD/CHF at 0.5729 with a December range of 0.5596-0.5824; another has the pair beginning December 2026 at 0.575 and finishing at 0.580), while the only constructible bank-derived cross (Goldman Sachs 10 January 2026 USD/CHF forecast of 0.76 combined with the Exchange Rates UK AUD/USD Q4-2026 survey consensus of 0.7148) implies AUD/CHF of roughly 0.5433 — some 262 pips below spot
consensus_divergence.our_strategic_view: 0.5775 at three months, 0.5800 at six months
consensus_divergence.divergence_direction: Above bank-derived cross consensus; roughly in line with the upper end of algorithmic model forecasts
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: +270 pips (+5.0%) above the bank-derived cross consensus of 0.5433 at the six-month horizon; approximately +70 pips above the centre of the model-forecast range of 0.571
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: We differ for three specific bilateral reasons. First, the sell-side franc forecasts are constructed from a USD/CHF and EUR/CHF view in which Swiss structural strength and a falling dollar dominate; they are not constructed from a carry view, and they therefore systematically understate what a 435bp differential does to a cross where the high-yielder is stable. Second, consensus treats the SNB's zero-rate commitment as protective of the franc when in practice it removes the currency's policy optionality, which is what reassigned it as a funding leg. Third, on the base leg, consensus underweights the specific mechanics of the 11 August SoMP, where the RBA must mark LNG and thermal coal assumptions to a spot complex running 91-114% above Treasury Budget parameters.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: Capturing the six-month move to 0.5800 plus 129.8 pips of carry delivers approximately +4.13% on a forward expression, against a consensus-implied path that would deliver roughly -2.5% before carry
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If the bank-derived view is correct and the franc's structural case reasserts through a volatility shock, the pair converges toward 0.5450 or below, costing 245 pips of spot against 130 pips of carry for a net -2.02%; the specific failure mode is a Middle East escalation past US$115 Brent, which would simultaneously validate the terms-of-trade bull case and destroy it through the risk channel

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons are aligned in direction and decaying in intensity, with overall confidence falling from 65% to 59%. The decay is fully explained by the weight schedule and by three factor reclassifications: Factors 2, 3 and 5 all fall from Bullish to Neutral as the horizon extends, removing +0.2136 of contribution, while Factor 8 additionally flips from Neutral to Bearish as relative Swiss sovereign quality becomes the substrate for haven demand. What holds the direction together is that Factor 1's 0.28 weight is unchanged across horizons and its stance is unchanged too — the one thing that does not decay is the differential itself.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The 24 September SNB monetary policy assessment. Before it, no scheduled event can change the Swiss leg, so the thesis runs largely unopposed. At it, the SNB revises its conditional inflation forecast for the first time since the energy shock re-intensified, and the residual 12-25bp of hawkish premium in the CHF front end either decays — extending the thesis — or is validated, which would mark the strategic turn. The transition catalyst to watch is Swiss headline CPI sustaining above 1.0% with core above 0.6%, which would flip Factor 1 to Neutral and Factor 6 to Neutral, a swing of roughly -0.27 on the strategic score, taking it to approximately -0.01 and conviction 1.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Carry the position with a tactical entry and a strategic stop, concentrating exposure in the four to six weeks before the September SNB assessment where the highest-quality part of the expected return sits, then reduce size unless the conviction ladder's increase conditions have been met. Practically, that argues for forwards maturing before the December year-end basis turn rather than through it, and for buying a small AUD/CHF downside hedge separately rather than reducing the core position.

catalysts.event: Swiss July Consumer Price Index (Federal Statistical Office)
catalysts.rationale: June printed +0.5% headline with SFSO core inflation 1 at 0.3%, and July faces an unfavourable energy base effect as the March-April Brent spike drops out of the annual comparison. A print at or below 0.4% revives negative-rate speculation and erodes the residual 12-25bp of hawkish SNB premium, widening the effective differential without any RBA action. A print above 0.8% with core above 0.5% is the mirror risk and would be the first credible threat to the pair's rate thesis.

catalysts.event: RBA Monetary Policy Board decision + August Statement on Monetary Policy
catalysts.rationale: The dominant event of the tactical window and the only one capable of moving the differential inside it. Market pricing is roughly a coin flip on a 25bp hike after the 29 July CPI undershoot, meaning the distribution runs from +435bp unchanged to +460bp with no compression path. Independently of the rate decision, the SoMP must mark terms-of-trade and export-price assumptions to a spot complex 91-114% above Treasury Budget parameters and abandon the May baseline's assumption of conflict resolution — worth an estimated 30-50 pips to the pair on its own. Retention of the conditional tightening clause is the key language marker.

June showed unemployment steady at 4.4% with employment up 76,300 and participation at 67.0%. Because the SNB is pinned to zero regardless of Swiss data, Australian labour data is the highest-frequency variable capable of moving this pair's differential. A rise above 4.6% would materially weaken the RBA's capacity-pressure diagnosis and remove the hiking option; a further tightening validates it.

catalysts.event: RBA Monetary Policy Board minutes (11 August meeting)
catalysts.rationale: Minutes carry the vote composition, which is not forecastable. May was 8-1 and June unanimous; a return to a split with dissents for a hike would reinstate the tightening expectations that the CPI undershoot removed, directly re-widening the differential. Second-order for most pairs but first-order for a pure carry cross where the differential is the entire thesis.

Q1 was +0.4% quarter-on-quarter on the sport-adjusted basis and Q2 is the first quarter capturing the full trade-uncertainty drag preceding tariff implementation, with Q2 real export growth of only +0.6% against +8.8% nominal. A print below 0.2% confirms EY's 0.6% annual growth forecast over the SNB's 'around 1%' and reinforces the franc's funding-leg status through the growth channel with no offsetting base-leg effect.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision + Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The transmission to this cross is indirect and two-sided, which is why it is Ambiguous rather than directional. A hike with a hawkish dot distribution pushes the dollar toward the 'US exceptionalism' leg of the smile, where AUD historically underperforms — bearish for the base leg — while simultaneously entrenching franc funding and widening the CHF-USD gap beyond 400bp — bearish for the quote leg. The net for AUD/CHF depends on which channel dominates, and the deciding variable is whether the hike arrives alongside risk-asset stability or a term-premium shock.

catalysts.event: SNB Monetary Policy Assessment and news conference
catalysts.rationale: The single largest scheduled quote-leg event of the strategic window and the identified thesis inflection point. The SNB revises its conditional inflation forecast — currently 0.6%/0.6%/0.7% conditioned on 0.00% throughout — for the first time since the energy shock re-intensified. A downward revision toward 0.4% or a restatement of the zero commitment decays the residual hawkish premium and extends the pair; an upward revision above 0.9% for 2027 validates the premium and is the first credible strategic threat. Watch also for any change to the 'increased willingness to intervene' language, which is the one-directional floor beneath the pair.

catalysts.event: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs extend to all non-Annex-III Swiss importers
catalysts.rationale: The 15% capped Swiss rate took effect on 31 July for the seventeen Annex III companies and captures all remaining importers from this date. Pharmaceuticals are Switzerland's largest export category to the United States, so this is the point at which the tariff drag becomes economy-wide rather than concentrated, compressing the current-account surplus that is the principal structural argument against a long AUD/CHF position.

catalysts.event: ABS Consumer Price Index, September quarter 2026
catalysts.rationale: The highest-impact single Australian release because of the quarterly cadence, compressing three months of expectations into one print. June showed headline at 3.8% with the trimmed mean flat at 3.6%; the September quarter captures the full pass-through of the July energy escalation into transport and input costs against base effects from the expiring electricity rebate distortion. This is the print that determines whether the differential holds at 435bp into 2027 or begins to compress from the base side.

catalysts.event: RBA Monetary Policy Board decision + November Statement on Monetary Policy
catalysts.rationale: The second full forecast round of the strategic window and the first RBA document to confront a materially compressed relative-rate position against most peers — but not against the SNB. CBA expects the RBA on hold through 2026 with two cuts in 2027, and the November SoMP is where any easing bias would first appear in the forecasts. For this pair specifically, an emerging RBA easing bias is the only base-side mechanism capable of compressing a differential that the quote side cannot compress.

A dated, binary trade-policy event that hits both legs in the same direction against the pair. AUD is the G10's most liquid China proxy with China taking approximately 30% of Australian exports at A$196bn, so a failure to extend transmits to the base leg faster than to any other currency, while the risk-off impulse simultaneously restores haven demand for the quote leg. This is one of the few catalysts where the base and quote effects compound rather than offset, which makes it disproportionately dangerous for a pure risk-proxy carry cross.

catalysts.event: SNB Monetary Policy Assessment + December Monetary Policy Report
catalysts.rationale: The SNB's most information-rich event of the year, and the point at which the market's residual hawkish premium (roughly +12bp priced for December on a stale snapshot) is either paid or unwound. It falls immediately before the December year-end cross-currency basis turn, compounding volatility for franc-funded positions in exactly the week when balance-sheet capacity is thinnest — the specific reason we prefer strategic forwards maturing before rather than through the turn.

catalysts.event: Strait of Hormuz developments and Brent crude path (undated, ongoing)
catalysts.rationale: The single most important undated catalyst and the one with a genuine inversion threshold specific to this pair. Below roughly US$115 Brent, energy strength is a terms-of-trade transfer from a net importer (Switzerland) to a net exporter (Australia) and the pair rises; above it, the market reclassifies energy as a risk event, the franc catches a haven bid, and the risk channel overwhelms the price channel because it moves both legs at once. Brent has ranged US$70.46 to US$126.69 in five months, so both branches are live.

assumptions: Spot and price-derived metrics: all spot, performance, 52-week range, range percentile, moving averages, trend regime and recent price-action narrative are taken from the provided Twelve Data daily OHLC series (390 observations, 12 June 2025 to 5 August 2026). Spot is the 5 August 2026 close of 0.5695. There is a four-day gap between the stated valuation date of 1 August 2026 and the latest price observation of 5 August; all levels, targets and pip calculations are stated relative to 0.5695, and the dossiers' own AUD/CHF reference of 0.56828 (31 July close) is used only where dossier-internal consistency requires it.

Implied volatility, risk reversals and barriers are unobservable for this pair: no free public venue publishes AUD/CHF at-the-money implied volatility, a volatility term structure, 25-delta risk reversals, or option barrier concentrations for mid-2026. The 1M and 3M implied figures used (5.8% and 6.3%) are our own estimates constructed from the two USD legs with a correlation adjustment; all skew inference is read across from observable EUR/CHF and USD/CHF risk reversals, which is directionally valid for the franc leg but says nothing about the AUD leg. This is the single largest data gap in the analysis.

Forward points are CIP-derived and cross-multiplied, not traded quotes: AUD/CHF forwards are constructed by multiplying the AUD dossier's CIP-derived AUD/USD forward outrights by the CHF dossier's USD/CHF forward outrights, then scaling the resulting annualised discounts to the price-data spot of 0.5695. Actual traded AUD/CHF forwards will differ by the cross-currency basis on both legs, which is unobservable this cycle.

Valuation is a REER-differential proxy, not absolute PPP: both dossiers construct their PPP tables from BIS real broad effective exchange rate deviations over a 30-month window rather than from absolute purchasing-power parity data, producing materially different AUD/CHF fair values (0.5336 and 0.5061) because each anchors on its own base currency's window mean. The 6.7%-12.5% overvaluation is treated as an ordinal statement rather than a point estimate.

Cross-currency basis is unobservable for both legs: neither 3M AUD/USD nor 3M USD/CHF basis could be sourced. Factor 10 is assessed without its primary instrument at both horizons, and any basis widening — particularly into the December year-end turn — is treated as a first-order invalidation signal this analysis cannot measure.

Bilateral trade uses the injected IMF DOTS block without re-estimation: the DOTS figures are internally inconsistent between reporting and mirror data, reflecting Switzerland's role as the world's largest gold refining hub. Both directions are reported as supplied, and bilateral trade is treated as immaterial to the pair's dynamics regardless of which figure is used.

Weight adjustment rationale: six factors were adjusted from default, none by more than ±0.04, with both columns summing to exactly 1.00. The two largest adjustments (Factor 1 +0.04, Factor 3 +0.04 tactical) are funded primarily by the reduction in Factor 10, which the framework explicitly identifies as appropriate for non-USD crosses.

Stance-to-score mapping and conviction ladder: Bullish = +1, Neutral = 0, Bearish = -1; confidence-adjusted score = stance × confidence/100; weighted contribution = confidence-adjusted score × weight. Conviction maps from absolute net score: below 0.10 = 1, 0.10-0.20 = 2, 0.20-0.35 = 3, 0.35-0.55 = 4, above 0.55 = 5. Tactical arithmetic reconciles to +0.5448 and 65.03%; strategic to +0.2597 and 59.35%.

Flagged figures carried from the dossiers: VIX at 17.09 (secondary check 17.64), Brent at US$91.82 (secondary sources span US$87.8-92.7), the Swiss AAA confirmation (379 days old) and 37.6% debt ratio (2024 vintage), the OIS-implied SNB path (57 days stale), the Swiss 2Y yield (single-sourced and internally inconsistent), and the EUR/CHF bank survey (53 days stale) are all carried forward with their original flags intact.

Consensus construction: no dated sell-side grid exists for AUD/CHF at 3M/6M/12M horizons. The bank-derived consensus of approximately 0.5433 is our own cross-multiplication of a 10 January 2026 Goldman Sachs USD/CHF forecast with the Exchange Rates UK AUD/USD survey consensus, and it is flagged as stale on the franc leg. The model-based forecasts cited are algorithmic rather than analyst-driven, and one (0.531 for end-July 2026) has already been invalidated by realised prices, which is disclosed rather than omitted.
